description: Run ObjectScript unit tests and measure which lines of the listed classes they execute. Use it to see how well a test target covers specific classes, and which lines of their source it misses. It returns the test summary (total, passed, failed, skipped, details) and the coverage twice. Per class and per method, over the class's own source lines (coverage.classes[].source): executable lines, covered lines, percent and the uncovered line ranges, plus the count of lines the compiler generated in the class, which are never reported as source lines; a method with a reason (generator, not-objectscript or layout) has no class-source lines, and neither has a method that compiles to no INT code, which carries no reason; a statement that spans several lines is one line, the first that maps to its code (for a multi-line &sql statement, the line after the &sql( line); a class whose definition changed after it was compiled, or whose compiled line map is gone (a documentation-only edit saved after the compile, which a default compile does not rebuild), has source.reason not-up-to-date. And per measured INT routine (coverage.classes[].routines[]): its executable line count, covered line count, percent and the executable and covered INT line ranges. A class that could not be measured is listed under coverage.unmeasured with a reason (not-compiled, no-routines or no-int-source). The text result is compact: one status line, the coverage target line when minCoverage was passed, one line per class with its uncovered ranges (and one indented line per method with an uncovered line), one line per routine, then the classes that were not measured. minCoverage (0 to 100) adds coverage.verdict to a completed result: a class passes when its unrounded ratio of covered to executable class lines is at least the minimum, fails below it or when it was not measured, and is notApplicable with no executable class line; overall passes when the unrounded total is at least the minimum and no class failed for want of a result. A failing verdict is still isError false. DEFAULT-DISABLED (it starts an instance-wide monitor session and runs test code): enable it with IRIS_GOVERNANCE={"global":{"iris_test_coverage":true}}. Operator control: IRIS_TEST_TIMEOUT (seconds) sets the default wait budget; the `timeout` argument overrides it per call (default 120 s, hard-capped at 3600 s; a larger value is clamped and the result carries timeoutCapped: true). Shared-instance guard: one coverage run at a time instance-wide. While any Line-by-Line or PERFMON session is running (this tool's own, or anyone else's), the call is refused with code MONITOR_BUSY and owner "suite" or "foreign"; nothing is started and a foreign session is never touched. TestProduction guard: a run that includes a %UnitTest.TestProduction test is refused with code PRODUCTION_BUSY, and nothing is run, while a production other than those tests' own is running in the namespace (or its state cannot be read), because %UnitTest.TestProduction stops any other production before it starts its own; that production is left untouched. The guard needs the ExecuteMCPv2 service at the version that ships it: on a server without it the run is unguarded. Only the process that runs the tests is measured (and the suite's own supervisor process, which runs only the suite's own classes, so they count only if you list them), so code that runs in processes the tests start is not counted. Coverage is INT-line coverage of the listed classes' routines, including the code the compiler generates in them (list 1 to 50 classes; the run is refused above 200,000 measured INT lines); a method that compiles to no INT code has no lines to cover. Class names are matched exactly as compiled, with the package and the letter case (for example MyApp.Orders). Class line numbers are those of the class document that iris_doc_get returns for '<class>.cls', which IRIS stores in its own layout (one blank line between members, each signature on one line): a file uploaded in another layout can number its lines differently, so read the class with iris_doc_get before comparing. INT line numbers (the routine lines) are different: INT line n is line n+1 of the document iris_doc_get returns for '<routine>.int' (for example 'MyApp.Orders.1.int') and of the text iris_routine_intermediate returns, whose line 1 is the ROUTINE header. If the wait budget expires while the run is still executing, the result is isError false with status "running", the run's coverageRunId and its handles: do NOT re-submit. Re-attach with iris_test_status (action "poll", coverageRunId), which returns the same result once the run is finished; its "cancel" action stops the run and is a key of its own, iris_test_status:cancel, also DEFAULT-DISABLED (enable it with IRIS_GOVERNANCE={"global":{"iris_test_status:cancel":true}}). A coverage handle is kept for the 20 most recent runs and does not survive an instance restart. A Cobertura XML file for CI tools is written by iris_test_status action "export" (coverageRunId, an absolute outputPath ending .xml), never by this tool; export is a write key of its own, also DEFAULT-DISABLED (enable it with IRIS_GOVERNANCE={"global":{"iris_test_status:export":true}}).

classes.description: The classes whose INT routines are measured: 1 to 50 class names, with no wildcards, written exactly as compiled (package-qualified, same letter case). A class that is not compiled in the namespace under that name is reported under coverage.unmeasured.

minCoverage.description: A coverage target, a number from 0 to 100. The run is stored with it, and a completed result carries coverage.verdict: each class is pass when its unrounded class-line ratio is at least the target, fail below it or when it was not measured, and notApplicable with no executable class line. The verdict never makes the result an error. Omit it for no verdict.

server.description: Named server profile to target for this call (from `IRIS_PROFILES`). Omit to use the default server.

target.description: Test target: package name (e.g., 'MyApp.Tests'), class name (e.g., 'MyApp.Tests.UtilsTest'), or class:method (e.g., 'MyApp.Tests.UtilsTest:TestSomething')

timeout.description: Maximum time to wait for the run, in SECONDS, before returning a 'running' result instead of blocking further (default: 120, or IRIS_TEST_TIMEOUT if set; hard-capped at 3600s - a larger value is clamped and the response carries timeoutCapped:true). MCP clients impose their own tools/call ceiling independently of this value (commonly 60s) - treat the running-result-plus-re-attach contract as the robust path for a slow suite.

name: iris_test_coverage
